what: Stage 1: the chip lockstep's scope file. For every command (the chip's mailbox table index, word bits 8-13) and every compared field, the reference the stage-1 firmware (FW_S1, our new firmware) is held to: 'chip' (the cart program in the cart-music runner, our test harness outside this tree), 'final026' (the host build of the final 0.2.6 firmware, passed on hardware), 'rule:<name>' (a fixed rule, no reference side), or 'off' (not compared, with the reason). A difference in a field whose reference is chip or final026 FAILS the run unless an exception below names its allow-list row and the exact case; transforms (chip writes of later stages) are counted per row, never silently dropped. Stages are the steps of the 0.3.0 work (docs/ALLOWLIST.md lists them); test build 4 and S3a are firmware builds B Jam tested on his hardware; D-numbers are the differences of our firmware audit (not in this tree). Read by tests/equiv/chiplock_s1.py.
labels: Rows are tests/equiv/allowlist.json ids (docs/ALLOWLIST.md). A row marked 'Z5 proposed' was in the stage-1 allow-list merge of 2026-10-13 and waited for B Jam's yes; 'none' = no row yet, listed in the chip lockstep's notes as a proposal.

chip_sites.what: the chip program's status helper stores ($1FE6, $1FE4: the rig records the helper's caller for them) and the job step's bit-14 store (the C6 transform)

regwrites.what: the MCU's register-file writes ($1FE0-$1FFF, chip 0x68040000 + offset) during the event, offset and value, in order (docs/CART_FPGA_SPEC.md 15.1). $1FE6 values compared without bits 3 and 13 (row B10's split: row B12 until stage 5), and ours must never set either. The chip's writes of later stages are removed by the transforms below (counted per row). Ours' board-only SPTR / GO / DEC_BASE entries and the host model's RTL-decoder GO are not compared here (rule go_after_start). Since 2026-10-15 (MCU interface v1.2): the flush's load-list pushes are compared write for write (the transform T-S2 is gone: our firmware pushes the list as the chip does).

stored.what: the MCU side of $1FE4, $1FE6, $1FEA, $1FEC after the event: what an MCU read returns (docs/CART_FPGA_SPEC.md R3; the chip's own read-backs, e.g. the heartbeat's bit-11 test). Equal stored words after every event make every MCU read of them equal. $1FE6 without bits 3 and 13 (row B10's split).

fe4_view.what: the 68000's $1FE4 = (busy << 2) | the Console model bits (option word bits 6, 8-10), every other bit 0 (docs/CART_FPGA_SPEC.md section 3.4, the $1FE4 composer; row B6); before the first stream GO busy = 1, so the word is 0x0004 | model, the value the game reads at $BCA22 (= final 0.2.6's word). Against final026: bit 2 masked (row B2), the rest equal.

status_view.what: the 68000's $1FE6, $1FEA, $1FEC: the stored words (the register file returns them as stored), so 'stored' covers them. Against final026: $1FE6 strict outside B10's bits (0xE708: bits 15, 14, 13, 10, 9, 8, 3), so bits 0-2 (A2) and the MegaWire bits 4 / 5 stay 0.2.6's; $1FEA / $1FEC and B10's bits are a change of reference, counted.

regpage_other.what: the 68000's $1FE0, $1FE2, $1FE8, $1FEE, $1FF0-$1FFE: the stage-1 register file reads 0 there (docs/CART_FPGA_SPEC.md C1, docs/MCU_INTERFACE.md 3.4); 0.2.6 left RAMDP words. The game reads only $1FE4, $1FE6, $1FEA. Counted per word, not failed.

go_after_start.what: docs/CART_FPGA_SPEC.md 15.1, test T4: every FIFO-B start ours writes ($1FF2 = 0xC002) is followed by a firmware GO in the same event; every decoder start ($1FF2 = 0x8000) with an entry queued has the board's DEC_BASE write after its last push and the RTL decoder's GO after it (MCU interface v1.2: the host board's model decodes at the START); checked by rule, not against the chip.

fifo_b.what: docs/CART_FPGA_SPEC.md 15.1, test T2 (allow-list row B4: the served bytes, never where they sit): after a post whose chip side fed FIFO B (DB06: the first chunk, up to 0x78 words from the chip's SDRAM; no refills without EXTI 12), those bytes against ours' workspace at SPTR for the GO's length. The chip's FIFO-B data reaches its SDRAM through its own unpack jobs (DA), so this compares the two decoders through the window.

ram_chip.what: the cart-RAM words a command fragment that works as the chip's writes itself (per command, list 'ram_chip_words'; 'ram_chip_when': job_queued = only when the post queued its job, as C6 writes them only then): compared with the chip's RAMDP after an accepted post (no refusal bit 9 / 10).

ramdp.what: cart RAM $0000-$1FDF after a mailbox-B post, every word, except the command's ram_chip words (a change of reference: B10 for C6, B26 for 84), $1E4 = $FF00 (B20, docs/BOOT_SPEC.md BOOT-06) and the sprite words (since the sprite-values update: 'sprite_words' below, a counted change of reference to the chip). The chip's audio and MegaWire RAM writes and the sprite rows still 0.2.6's are later stages (B12, B5, B14) and are never compared with the chip here.

sprite.what: the sprite-values update (B Jam's decision of 2026-10-15/16; section 4.1 of our sprite-values specification, not in this tree): the sprite words the game reads as data, against the chip after every accepted post of the commands whose entry names 'sprite_chip': AD ($1F10, $1F16, $1F18, $1F1A) and AF ($1F10, $1F16, $1F18, $1F1A, $1F1C; the AF's DMA descriptors, every word, from the $1F16 before the post to the new one; SAT entries 0-129 and the stash $1F20-$1F8F (14 entries), every word: since test build 4 D23 is done the chip's way, the chip's attribute ADD and pose bit 29, so the attribute word is held to the chip too (until test build 4 masked to Y, link and X, the attribute word under B14)). No allowance: SAT entry 0 after an AF that leaves the table empty was forgiven until stage 2 (the runner's boot page and 0.2.6's B1 clear of entry 0, D47, never shown); stage 2 does D47 the chip's way, the allowance was used 0 times on every corpus, and stage 2's repair (2026-10-28) retired it. See 'sprite_words' for the final026 side.

pointer.what: the stream-window pointer after the post (0.2.6 sdram_ptr, stage-1 SPTR)

volumes.what: the low byte of VOL_SFX / VOL_BGM

audio.what: the album / SFX entry points with their arguments (A4: compared at the call interface; B12 against the chip until stage 5)

bram.what: the battery save $000-$8FF after every post that can touch it (C6, DF, E0, 84, 85) and at every checkpoint; $900-$FFF strict in RELEASE, A1 in TEST; $1000-$1FFF (B33: the 8 KB save) must stay 0 in RELEASE, A1 (the debug record) in TEST

sdram.what: the 2 MB workspace at every checkpoint (default every 1,000 frames) and at the end: the bytes the window serves come from it (B4: against the chip only the served bytes count, never where they sit)

transforms.what: the 9494 tick's FIFO-A packet: $1FF0 written at the TIM14 flush (the Z80 music packet into RAMDP $1800, stage 5)
the synth's $1FE6 bit-13 set: no chip value before stage 5
the main loop's $1FE6 bit-3 store (music playing): the sequencer is stage 5
the MegaWire bodies of A6 / A9: $1FE6 bits 5 / 4 cleared
the MegaWire task's status block (81 bit 3, the main loop's TIM7-rate task)
the MegaWire init's status writes inside the C6 job (bit 14, bits 5 / 4 / 0 / 1 / 2)
in the C6 event, the job-step bit-14 stores (caller 0x0801A608) of the jobs that end while the MegaWire init's job 6 is still queued: all but the last
the EEPROM driver's $1FE4 bit-11 writes (the chip's save format and its driver are stage 3)
docs/CART_FPGA_SPEC.md 15.1, test T2: the FIFO-B refill writes ($1FF2 at 0x0801D548 / 0x0801D582; none without EXTI 12)

exceptions.row: B6 (MegaWire On is a labelled difference: decision 6 of our firmware plan, B Jam 2026-10-09, On keeps 0.2.6's signed-in look; B6's scope names $1FE6 bits 0-2 only, widening it to bits 4 / 5 is a W13 proposal)
exceptions.case: MegaWire On (option word bits 16-18), from the first accepted E7 on
exceptions.what: The chip's E7 (0x0801C3FA-0x0801C46A) moves the message into its send buffer, sets $1FE6 bit 4 (send pending), zeroes RAMDP $1C10, clears bit 5 (data in); its MegaWire task clears bit 4 again when the send ends (0x08021A9C; with no module, two frames later in the attract capture). Stage 1 keeps 0.2.6's E7 ('pretend data is in': bit 5 set, $1C10 := the length + 16), which never clears: the signed-in look. With MegaWire On, from the first E7 on, $1FE6 bits 4 / 5 are masked on both sides and a $1FE6 write that changes only them is dropped, counted. The game posts E7 only when $1FE6 bits 0-2 != 0 (from our completeness check of the commands, finding 8); the attract capture was recorded with status 7 and is replayed with MegaWire On. With MegaWire Off there is no exception: the chip's no-module path is the reference and a difference FAILS (measured: attract replayed with Off fails with 241,212 differences, 120,618 register-write and 120,594 stored-word, the first at the first E7, frame 5142; the same replay passes when only $1FE6 bits 4 / 5 are masked after an E7).

sprite_words.what: since the sprite-values update: the sprite words, chip-referenced at AD / AF (field 'sprite') and a counted change of reference against final 0.2.6 (allow-list B14: from the update on D24, D10, D38 and the rest of D42 are the chip's, so 80+ frames, the extra entries of pieces above or below the screen, the second 14-entry DMA and the stash differ from 0.2.6 by design). Against final026 a word of these groups (the SAT, the DMA list, the stash, the four words) may start to differ only at a post of a command that writes it the chip's way here ('diverge_at'); it is then not compared with final026 (counted, per post) until both sides hold the same value again; a word that starts to differ at any other post FAILS ('ramdp_sprite').
sprite_words.dma_note: all 121 descriptor slots: the game's list reaches past $1800 in busy screens (measured: solo frame 1,744, AF descriptors at slots 65-66), where it overlaps the audio page 88 fills and C6 clears ($1800 / $1802, B10: diverge_at 06)
sprite_words.chip_sat_words_note: the words of each SAT / stash entry held to the chip after an AF (0 Y, 1 size / link, 2 the attribute word, 3 X; tests/equiv/sprwords.py): since test build 4 D23 is done the chip's way (B Jam's decision of 2026-10-18), so all four; until test build 4 [0, 1, 3]
sprite_words.diverge_note: a group name lets every word of that group start to differ at that command, an address that one word; C6's $1800 / $1802 := 0 is B10 (until the game's next 88 rewrites them); stage 2: B1 (the chip's flush only, D47) leaves SAT entry 0 as it was, where final 0.2.6 cleared it with an empty table

default.final026_note: 0.2.6 printed 'unknown'; the chip refuses with $1FE6 bit 9 (B) / 10 (A): B28 (Z5 proposed), a status-word difference only
